description: We're a team of 4 who care about making science accessible to everyone, no matter how they see, hear, or learn. We believe NASA's data shouldn't depend on one sense, and we want to build something that opens up Earth science to people who are often left out, including blind and low-vision users. We value inclusive design, testing with real users, and clear communication.
summary:
A.T.L.A.S. (Acoustic Technology & Listening Astronomy System) is a web and Android app that turns NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) climate visualizations into real-time music, vibration and voice, so blind and low-vision people can explore Earth's changing climate with one finger.

NASA's Earth data is shared almost entirely as coloured maps. A screen reader can read a map's caption, but not the map itself. A.T.L.A.S. reads the pixel under the user's finger, turns its colour back into a value using NASA's official legend, and plays it as sound: ocean is a soft pad, land is a harp, xylophone or flute, higher values are higher notes, coastlines click and vibrate, and anomalies pulse. A resting finger hears the name of the place; a double tap speaks the exact value.

Users can travel through time (same month every year, 2003–2024), switch between temperature, wildfires, sea ice and the CO2 Keeling curve, and zoom into continents. Built for blind users first, it works with VoiceOver and TalkBack, by keyboard, and in English and Russian, turning the challenge's "sight into sound" into an experience anyone can explore.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

A.T.L.A.S. is an interactive "Earth Jukebox" that pairs NASA EIC climate visuals with sonification generated in real time. It has three ways to listen:

- Explore: slide a finger (or mouse, or arrow keys) across a NASA map and hear what is under it.

- Time travel: two-finger swipes move through the same month in different years, so users hear climate change rather than seasons.

- CO2 curve: the Mauna Loa Keeling curve (1958–2026) plays as a rising 20-second melody with spoken milestones.

HOW IT WORKS

Three independent engines communicate only through events:

1. Vision reads the pixel under the finger and converts its colour back into a number using the layer's NASA GIBS colour legend. A Natural Earth land mask detects coastlines.

2. Sound turns that number into a note on a C minor pentatonic scale (so no gesture sounds wrong), picks an instrument by surface and theme, and places it in 3D stereo space (left of the map in the left ear).

3. Touch and voice vibrates at coastlines, ice edges and anomalies (Android), plays clicks instead on iPhone, and speaks region names and values.

DATA

Themes follow NASA's Earth Information Center. Dated frames come from NASA GIBS/Worldview: MODIS Land Surface Temperature (July 2003–2024), MODIS Fires and Thermal Anomalies (August 2003–2024) and AMSR2 Sea Ice Concentration (September 2012–2024): 23 frames, 7 continents and 15 named regions. Headline values come from NASA GISTEMP v4, the NSIDC Sea Ice Index and NOAA GML / Scripps CO2 records. We acknowledge the use of imagery provided by services from NASA's Global Imagery Browse Services (GIBS), part of NASA's Earth Science Data and Information System (ESDIS).

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

43 million people worldwide are blind (The Lancet Global Health, 2021), and climate is almost always explained with colour. Tactile maps are slow and expensive and need a new print for every year and dataset. A.T.L.A.S. runs on any phone, changes year and theme with a swipe, and gives blind students, teachers, researchers and the public the same NASA data a sighted scientist sees.

ACCESSIBILITY

Two voice modes (screen reader mode for VoiceOver/TalkBack and a self-voicing mode), every control speaks, full keyboard control, English and Russian, light and dark themes. No accounts and no tracking; settings stay on the device.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

JavaScript web app with Tone.js (Web Audio) for synthesis, sampling and 3D sound; the Vibration API and Web Speech; a small server that calls ElevenLabs for a natural voice so the API key never reaches the browser (it falls back to the phone's built-in voice); hosted on Vercel, with an Android APK. 253 automated tests (Vitest), about 97% line coverage of the app logic.

CREATIVITY

Most sonifications are fixed audio clips of one chart. A.T.L.A.S. lets users explore whole satellite maps with their own finger, combining music, haptics and spoken orientation, and puts a time-series chart in the same interface.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Honesty about data (values are read from map colours and rounded to legend steps; official series are quoted for headline numbers; the wildfire trend is an estimate from frames), musicality (pentatonic scale, smoothed changes), mobile performance, and real screen-reader workflows. We have not yet run a formal study with blind users; that is our first next step.

USE OF AI (SUPER INTELLIGENCE)

- Code and text: we used Claude (Anthropic) to help plan the project.

- Audio: the app's natural voice is AI-generated speech from ElevenLabs text-to-speech.

- All sonification (notes, rhythm, mapping) is generated by our own code from NASA data in real time. Instrument samples and sound effects are recordings under CC BY 3.0 and CC0, not AI-generated.
